Subject: Coordinating deep-dive: SE + Architects across US / EU / APAC

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for taking this on. We're keen to do a technical deep-dive where our platform architects (Sven in CH and our US team) pair with your SEs to validate latency patterns, KV cache behavior, and routing/fallbacks for a multi-region deployment. Our priorities:
- live inference run through (30–45m)
- data handling & audit logs (15m)
- rollout/rollback & canary plan (15m)

Constraint: our EU architect (Sven) is only available between 09:00–18:00 CEST; our US architects are 09:00–17:00 ET; APAC participants prefer not to be after 23:00 SGT. With DST differences next month we're getting tripped up scheduling.

Proposed windows (local times included):
- Option A: 13:00–14:30 UTC (US morning / EU afternoon / APAC late evening)
- Option B: 15:00–16:30 UTC (US late morning / EU late afternoon / APAC night)
- Option C: two back-to-back 60m sessions split US/EU+APAC friendly

I've attached a draft agenda (ATB-deep-dive-agenda_v1.pdf) and a quick note from Sven on constraints. Can you propose firm slots (with UTC conversions) and whether Redwood can accommodate a two-session fallback?

Thanks,
Kate
Kate Taylor
Head of Platform Partnerships
Atlas Bank

Hi Kate — great to meet you over email.

Thanks for the constraints and the agenda. I pulled together a small matrix with UTC conversions and three concrete overlap windows that respect the blocks you mentioned; attaching timezone_matrix_atb.xlsx. Short answers up front: we can do a single 90m session or split into two 60m sessions — both workable. My recommended windows (with quick pros/cons):

- Window 1 (preferred): 14:00–15:30 UTC — US (10:00–11:30 ET), EU (16:00–17:30 CEST), APAC (22:00–23:30 SGT). Pros: favours EU and US daylight hours; APAC late but still same day.
- Window 2: 15:00–16:30 UTC — US (11:00–12:30 ET), EU (17:00–18:30 CEST), APAC (23:00–00:30 SGT). Pros: slightly later EU; con: APAC crosses midnight for some locales.
- Window 3 (two-part): 13:00–14:00 UTC (US morning + EU afternoon) and 21:00–22:00 UTC for APAC-heavy follow-up if needed. Pros: avoids pushing APAC too late in single block; con: requires two commits.

Notes: DST transition in the US is on 2026-11-01 and EU on 2026-10-25 — currently both regions are on DST, but if you plan rolling sessions into Oct/Nov we'll need to re-evaluate.

Next steps I suggest: please confirm preferred window (1, 2, or two-part), call out final attendee names and their timezones, and confirm whether you'd like us to record the live runs and share traces/logs after the session.

I've cc'd Diego (our lead SE) and Marcus (team lead). If you'd like, Diego can propose an exact runbook for the inference demo.

Thanks — Jasmine
Jasmine Liu

Thanks, Jasmine & Kate. Quick operational comments:

- Our preferred single-slot is Window 1 (14:00–15:30 UTC). That gives us a clean 90m block to do a full run (30–45m live gen, 20m logs/trace walk-through, 25m Q&A).
- If APAC attendance is mandatory live, I support the two-part approach so we don't force a midnight session.
- We'll need 1–2 sample prompt/asset sets from Atlas 48 hours before the demo to pre-seed KV caches and warm quantized models for realistic perf. Can you confirm?

Proposed logistics if Window 1 is chosen:
- Zoom (record): https://zoom.us/j/9876543210?pwd=bridge
- Shared folder for traces & prep: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0AExampleSharedDrive/ATB-deep-dive
- Runbook draft I'll post by EOD tomorrow once I validate model variant and expected sequence lengths.

If anyone on the Atlas side prefers a later EU-friendly time, call it out and we can try Window 2 but bow to your architects' availability.

Cheers,
